rules.summary: The prospectus excludes US persons from subscribing unless the board or management company decides otherwise. Its definition of US person is mixed: a residence- and incorporation-based list, a catch-all for Regulation S Rule 902, and a carve-out for 'Non-United States persons' under CFTC Rule 4.7. US citizenship or US tax status alone does not exclude: US taxpayers may subscribe if they are not US persons.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.
Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S

rules.summary: BI-EUR is core class I, which the prospectus reserves to institutional investors. These are defined as investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law: credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for others (including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement), insurance companies, pension funds and other UCIs. Contradiction: the BI-EUR KID says the fund is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels.

citations.quote: I Institutional investors. Yes None

institutional investors Investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law, such as credit institutions and other financial professionals investing on the behalf of themselves or other investors (whether retail in connection with a discretionary management agreement or institutional), as well as insurance companies, pension funds, or other UCIs.
The latter case could happen for an institutional share class of any fund for any period during which an investor not entitled to hold institutional shares was found to have held such shares.
